about: Stop 5 on the map page (the gardens question): the two candidates in UTM metres (E, N) and German-zero levels like map-plan.json. Koldewey's vaulted building as its own block in the South Palace's north-east corner, the North Palace on its +15 m terrace with its courts and principal rooms, and one guessed garden on the edge terraces the map already holds (gardens-edge-1 to 4). Plans read off sheet S3.45 (Uppsala, CC BY 4.0) and printed sizes; every height above a measured floor, every wall top, the stairs and every plant are ours, and say so.

vaulted.src: S3.45 read off (plus or minus 2 m): the cells' block either side of the central passage, a slightly irregular quadrangle at 445744 to 445767 E, 3600761 to 3600790 N, the corridor round it, the outer wall, the west range and the south range with the stair room; about 1,500 m2 drawn (P2021 p. 101: a half-basement of about 1,600 m2); turned with the palace's north and east walls
vaulted.hsrc: floor +4.6, walls founded at +0.8 (P2021 p. 101), both under the palace floor (+12); the roof is ours (REC bab.vaulted.upper): an earth roof at +12.4 just over the palace floor, the cells' block a step higher at +13.0, a parapet to +13.3 on the drawn outline; no garden on it (REC bab.vaulted.roofgarden: words only)

courts.src: West Courtyard on S3.45, 33.1 x 35.4 m (P2021 p. 126: 33 x 35 m)
East Courtyard on S3.45, 34.7 x 37.1 m (P2021 p. 126: 34 x 37 m)

halls.src: the West Courtyard's principal room on S3.45, 21.9 x 8.7 m (P2021 p. 126: 21 x 9 m)
the East Courtyard's principal room on S3.45, 31.1 x 11.3 m (P2021 p. 126: 31 x 11 m)

northPalace.hsrc: the main floor +15 (P2021 p. 118); the rooms' roofs at the map's +20 and the principal rooms raised to +24 are ours (REC bab.northpalace.main.body: a height as a fact never); roofs of cedar, fir and cypress beams and blue-glazed crenellations are named in the king's texts and not drawn this round

terraces.src: the map's edge terraces gardens-edge-1 to 4 (Pedersén's model levels +13, +11, +8, +4 on the terrace sections 22 m north and 48 m west of the building, P2021 p. 117 to 118, fig. 3.23, 3.32: 'only preliminary attempts'); the strips below are their visible tops

stairs.src: ours: one flight down each step on the west side, on the palace's middle line; Pedersén's model shows none
ours: one flight down each step on the north side, running along the wall where the strips are only 6 m wide

ground.src: the ground round the edge terraces at the canal's embankment, plus or minus 0 (P2021 p. 115: the terrace top +15 and the embankment ±0 'within a limited area some 22 m wide'); the map's ground field stood at +11 to +14 here and buried the terraces. Its south side is the inner walls' line, its east the terrace's east edge; outside it the ground climbs back to the map's field at one in two (ours). On the map page only

planting.src: every plant ours (REC bab.gardens.plants, bab.green.*: Guessed). Berossus: terraces planted with all manner of trees; the Nineveh garden relief (BM 124939, a type, never Babylon): trees in close regular rows on a slope; Sheldon 1924 (an illustration): trees on every terrace edge, creepers over plain brick edges, palms at the water. Kinds as types: date palm (palm-date-babylon), cypress, broad aromatic and fruit trees, a few pomegranates, one fig; vines and caper hanging from the edges (GREEN H). April: the deciduous kinds in new leaf

hanging.src: vine curtains and caper mounds over the terraces' own edges only, never a documented wall (GREEN H; REC bab.green.hanging, bab.green.vine)

door.opens: the oil list and its peoples (feature 2, src/wings/babylon/oil/) and gardens in words of their time (feature 3, src/wings/babylon/garden-words/), two close looks on paper
door.src: the stop's two presses as one group where the frozen designs put the one control (the lower right corner of the wide frame; centred inside the thumb's reach upright), each named by what it shows and never 'Learn more' (the words are the writer's); colour: the point of the held frame feature 3's colour panel settles on, the terraces (fractions of the frame), and how far it closes in (zoom, at least 1); today's camera: it moves with the stop's next round
